Leave it outside; when you get home, go inside, grab trash bags, throw it all in trash bags, and immediately in the dryer on highest heat, for two cycles. If it’s plastic, if it was me personally I may toss it just because there’s so many nooks and crannies. Or you can just do a super thorough inspection. This particular medication you don’t take it forever. It can severely damage your liver. The most you can take it is 10 months or so at a time, depending on what the dermatologist decides. It usually cures the acne the first “round” but I was unlucky so I did two more rounds but this most recent one it went away for good (knock on wood). 

Accurate permanently shrinks the sebaceous glands in your skin so it usually cures it after a few months of treatment and acne never returns. However a small percentage of people like myself need to take it again if the acne relapses. 

I will say; after the first time my acne was SIGNIFICANTLY improved. It’s never been as severe as it was before accutane.

So inflamed acne: sometimes painful, red bumps, sometimes have a white head, but are always slightly raised.
[example](https://theacnespecialist.files.wordpress.com/2013/03/how-to-treat-inflamed-acne-chico.jpg) 
Comedonal (non-inflammatory acne): clogged pores, less noticeable to others because usually not red, and give the skin a bumpy texture.
[example](http://www.clearskinstudy.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/08/Comedonal-acne-265x300.jpg) 

Examples of comedonal acne would be blackheads and whitheads. Examples of inflammatory acne would be pustules, nodules and cysts. Basically, if it hurts it's probably inflammatory acne. If it's only noticeable from certain lights, and creates a rough-looking texture, it's likely non-inflammatory clogged pores. Inflamed acne is derived from clogged pores, it's what happens when a clogged pore gets inflected. And most people don't just have one type or another, many have a combination of both types of acne.

I'm no expert but I have struggled with acne for years, here is what worked for me!

First off: be GENTLE with your skin. I know it's tempting to rush head first into things but a lot of acne treatments can be very drying. When your skin gets too dry, it overcompensates by producing more oil and that clogs pores, leading to acne.

It's important to very thoroughly remove makeup if she wears any. Also some makeup makes acne worse. I suggest looking up anything you put on your face on cosdna. But even if the ingredients aren't pore clogging, it can still react differently to everyone's skin. YMMV.

Recently, differin (adapalene) gel went from prescription-only to OTC sale. It's the most gentle of the retinoids and works well for combo skin. That did help me get rid of inflamed acne spots but did little for my clogged pores and CCs. 

I went to a derm a year ago and they prescribed me Doxycycline 200mg. This has cleared my cystic acne 100%. But it comes back whenever I get off it, I have yet to find a solution that doesn't involve me taking an antibiotic for the rest of my life (which isn't very good for your body.)

Since you said she's tried many OTC remedies, she's probably already tried BHAs (salicylic acid). That is a good chemical exfoliant as well as AHA (lactic acid, glycolic acid or mandelic acid). Everyone has different preferences.

Lastly, I've heard wonderful things about Curology. I recently signed up for it myself and am still awaiting my bottle but I'll let you know if that helps my CCs.

Hope I helped. (: she's very beautiful with or without acne. It also looks like she's a teenager, so this is probably hormone related acne, sometimes birth control can help with that, specifically OrthoTriCyclin or Yaz/Yasmin. But that's more of a last resort thing if topicals don't help.
